name: m4-uniques-3g

variantDescriptions.weak: `claude/uniques-audit` `41986b33ea` (retronym/scala#212 + #239 + census probe, census off) with today's `WeakHashSet` table
variantDescriptions.chunked: the same build, `ChunkedInterner(weak = false)`: no `WeakReference`, types live until the run ends
variantDescriptions.uncache-all: chunked-weak, and types made in the weak scopes are not interned (shared only if already in the table or a 4096-slot direct-mapped cache)

description: Do the uniques layouts matter more under heap pressure? At 8 GB on the M4 (job 557, separate forks) times are flat within ±1.5%. GC pauses are only about 3% of a fork, and uncache-all cuts them 35% (4,855 to 3,179 ms per fork). Chunk rejuvenation adds young GCs (49 vs 41) and pauses, so it is dropped. Here the heap is 3 GB: an 8 GB fork's occupancy after GC peaks at 4 GB, and one compile allocates 6.3 GB.
